rationale_summary: The TAKE IT DOWN Act is dominantly framed around consumer_public_safety, targeting exploitation, abuse, harassment, extortion, and concrete psychological, financial, and reputational harm to individuals—with heightened protection for minors—through federal criminalization and FTC unfair-and-deceptive-practices platform takedown enforcement. Consumer_public_safety edges out fundamental_rights because the statute anchors liability in tangible victim harm, child protection, anti-extortion, and consumer-protection UDAP enforcement rather than constitutional-rights declarations. Fundamental_rights is a strong secondary frame grounded in affirmative voluntary consent, reasonable expectations of personal privacy, and free-expression carve-outs for matters of public concern.
